segments.text: Today's lesson is going to be a fun one.
Today we step into a cozy Russian kitchen.
Our word of the day is хлеб.
It sounds a little like love if you stretch your imagination.
The Russians often say хлеб when they mean the stuff of life.
Now we build more kitchen words that go with хлеб.
It starts with mala like malt.
Яблока almost sounds like ямиблока, a crunchy block of fruit.
Это красная яблока, это красная яблока.
Here is sour, sour, say sour like sour.
Imagine a fancy sour offering you cheese.
Моясо has my, my favorite meat.
Our next word is soup, soup, soup.
It is basically the same word as English soup, an easy win.
Горячий суп, горячий суп, hot soup.
Чай с сахаром, чай с сахаром, ти вытшугар.
Now we learn a describing word.
Remember home from a few lessons ago?
Now picture a kitchen inside that house.
Our last kitchen word is еду.
In Russian every now belong to a team.
The teams are called masculine, feminine or neuter.
These teams change how we say describing words.
This is why we say вкусный хлеб.
This is why we say вкусное яблоко.
English does not change adjectives for teams.
But Russian gives every now and its own team color.
In Russia bread is treated with great respect.
It is often placed in the center of the table.
Bread is the head of everything.
Guests are welcomed with bread and salt.
Do you remember what хлеб means?
For kids, draw your favorite meal and label three items using today's words.
For adults, next time you make breakfast, say the rice mimimi is out loud for everything on your plate.
Now here is something really cool about one of today's words.
Want to know secret about чай?
Did you know that the Russian word чай
and the English word t are actually cousins from the same ancient route?
This word started in China as чай.
It traveled along the Silk Road through Persian and Turkish traders.
It finally arrived in Russian in the 17th century when tea became popular at the royal court.
Be careful though, the Russian word magazine sounds like magazine, but actually means shop.
Next time you see pack-up of tea, remember it's cousin чай.
They both come from the same Chinese route.
That connection is your secret shortcut to remembering it forever.
Remember every expert started as a beginner practicing today's words out loud,
even just once and you'll be amazed how fast you learn.
And if you'd rather watch them, listen, find us on YouTube at NerrorAreYou.
